articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Addresses Raptors Fans With Emotional Message Before Return
articles.summary: Seven years after delivering a historic championship, the Board Man reflects on enduring memories while preparing to lead a new era in Toronto.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard has never been one to say much about himself publicly, which made the video he released Tuesday ahead of his return to the Toronto Raptors stand out.

Seven years after leaving the Raptors following their championship run, Leonard is back in the city where he delivered the biggest season in franchise history. And while he has downplayed the attention surrounding Wednesday's home opener against the Chicago Bulls, his message to Raptors fans offered a glimpse of what the return means to him.

"People move on. Things change, and even the greatest moments become memories," Leonard said in the video, as footage from Toronto's 2019 championship run played behind him. "But some things, some things stay with you. What we shared here, that's forever."

The video revisits the championship parade and the Raptors' series-clinching victory over the Golden State Warriors. Leonard's message acknowledges the time that's passed without spending the entire video looking backward. He closes by talking up Toronto's young roster and the possibility of making another run at a title.

That last part is where the expectations come in.

Leonard's first stint in Toronto lasted just one season, but it ended with him winning Finals MVP and leading the franchise to its first NBA championship. The Raptors moved on after he chose to join the Los Angeles Clippers in free agency, and the two sides spent seven seasons apart before Toronto brought him back in an offseason trade.

Now 35, Leonard returns after potentially his best offensive regular season. His health remains an important consideration, but he has said he is feeling good after gradually ramping up during training camp.

Leonard also recognizes that preparing for a long season requires a different approach than it did earlier in his career. Speaking to reporters earlier this week, he said recovery has become a bigger priority as he has gotten older.

"You aren't 20 years old anymore, so recovery is big," Leonard said, according to Ryan Wolstat of the Toronto Sun .

For Toronto, the hope is that Leonard can help Scottie Barnes and the rest of the roster compete for another deep playoff run. The team surrendered Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and multiple draft assets to reacquire him, showing how much it believes his presence can change its outlook.

Leonard, meanwhile, doesn't seem particularly interested in making Wednesday night bigger than it needs to be. Asked whether he had thought much about the reception awaiting him, he brushed off the question, reminding reporters that Toronto has 41 regular-season home games before any potential playoff run.

"The fanbase is always great here," Leonard said, via Wolstat. "But this is going to be more than one game."

His video offered a more personal message than his comments to reporters typically do. The challenge now is turning that reunion into something that lasts beyond opening night.

Leonard believes the first championship wasn't luck. With the Raptors preparing to begin a new season, he has another chance to show what this group can accomplish together.

articles.title: Pidió un carro por aplicación y fue hallado muerto con signos de tortura: el último rastro de Freddy Blanco
articles.standfirst: Ingeniero desaparecido en Bogotá es hallado sin vida con signos de tortura
articles.summary: Ingeniero desaparecido en Bogotá es hallado sin vida con signos de tortura
articles.body: La inseguridad y la violencia en Bogotá cobran una nueva y desgarradora víctima. Se trata de Fredy Eduardo Blanco, un ingeniero de 33 años que fue reportado como desaparecido tras solicitar un servicio de transporte por aplicación y que, lamentablemente, fue hallado sin vida con brutales signos de tortura en una vivienda ubicada en la localidad de Ciudad Bolívar. De acuerdo con la información revelada por las autoridades y medios de comunicación como City TV, los hechos se remontan al pasado viernes 9 de octubre. Ese día, tras salir de la casa de su compañera sentimental, Blanco abordó un vehículo particular de color rojo que había solicitado a través de una aplicación móvil con rumbo a su domicilio. Desde ese momento, su familia perdió todo tipo de contacto con él. Las llamadas y mensajes de sus allegados no obtuvieron respuesta durante todo el fin de semana. No fue sino hasta el martes 13 de octubre cuando la incertidumbre dio paso a la tragedia: las autoridades confirmaron el hallazgo de su cuerpo en el interior de un inmueble en Ciudad Bolívar. Las imágenes captadas por cámaras de seguridad de la zona se han convertido en la pieza fundamental de la investigación. En los videos se observa el momento exacto en que el ingeniero se sube al automotor, un registro que ahora es analizado minuciosamente por la Fiscalía General de la Nación para dar con el paradero del conductor y esclarecer la ruta que tomó el vehículo. El panorama con el que se encontraron los investigadores y la propia familia al ubicar el cuerpo fue desolador. El ingeniero presentaba múltiples heridas con arma blanca, estaba atado de pies y manos y evidenciaba graves signos de tortura. Las primeras hipótesis de las autoridades apuntan a que Blanco habría sido blanco de una peligrosa organización delincuencial que opera bajo la modalidad de hurto o secuestro exprés en la ciudad. Paralelamente, versiones preliminares de la investigación señalan que los arrendatarios de la vivienda donde fue abandonado el cadáver —quienes serían de nacionalidad extranjera— habrían abandonado el lugar de manera repentina días antes del hallazgo. La madre de la víctima, Rosiris Palacio, expresó su profundo dolor a través de los medios de comunicación y exigió a las autoridades que el crimen no quede en la impunidad. "Yo hablé con él la última vez el viernes en la mañana, luego estuve marcándole el viernes por la tarde, el sábado nada, ya no me contestó más, ni domingo ni lunes", relató con angustia. Añadió además: "Yo sé que conociendo quién lo hizo, quién fue el que hizo esto, no me lo van a devolver, pero por lo menos quedo conforme con saber que se hizo justicia". Por su parte, organismos de seguridad y policía judicial continúan recolectando testimonios, analizando material probatorio y cruzando datos de geolocalización para desmantelar la red criminal detrás de este atroz homicidio que hoy enluta a la ingeniería y a la ciudadanía bogotana.

articles.title: ESPN insider blasts Lakers' Luka Doncic over one major flaw he must fix this season in LA
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are entering year three with Luka Doncic. However, being the leader of the organization now, he is going to have to fix one fatal flaw...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are officially entering the post-LeBron James era, as he made his debut with the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night. Now, all eyes are on Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves as they look to take the reins of the franchise.

Doncic saw some action during the preseason, but LA was primarily focused on keeping him rested for the regular season. It is also worth noting that Doncic received a technical foul during the preseason.

"Annnnnnnnd we have a preseason technical foul on Luka Doncic. You may recall Luka getting suspended for techs last spring," The Athletic's Law Murray wrote.

Doncic has enjoyed his first two seasons with the Lakers, and this one doesn't seem like it will be any different. The guard has been vocal this offseason about his feelings toward LA. Just hours before the team's season opener against the Golden State Warriors , Doncic sent a message to the fans.

"Dear LA, Tonight we start our run for a championship. Every player dreams of holding that trophy. To do it for all of you amazing fans would mean everything to us," Doncic said.

The superstar wants to give his all for the Lakers this season and prove he has what it takes to lead the team. Doncic is also aiming to play in every game this season. However, after he publicly made that goal clear, ESPN's Brian Windhorst criticized him for how often he argues with officials.

"When you say 'I'm not gonna take a night off', are you going to take possessions off because you're complaining to the officials," Windhorst said.

Last season, Doncic was suspended for a game after exceeding the NBA's technical foul limit during the regular season. With the veteran already picking up a technical for arguing with a referee during the preseason, it highlights one of the biggest areas of his game that needs improvement.

Playing every night could increase the risk of accumulating more technical fouls, especially given his tendency to argue with officials. Doncic needs to show real growth in this area, particularly if he wants the Lakers to succeed this season.

articles.title: Ravens are predicting big Trey Hendrickson revenge game vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Ravens players have a lot to say about Trey Hendrickson's shot at the Bengals this week.
articles.body:
The Trey Hendrickson revenge narratives are alive and well this week as the Cincinnati Bengals get ready to take on the Baltimore Ravens.

Just ask Hendrickson's Ravens teammates.

In the first media sessions of Week 7, multiple Ravens players brought up Hendrickson's first crack at the Bengals .

Veteran Calais Campbell noted that he's going to do whatever it takes to open things up so Hendrickson can have a big game.

Campbell said the following, courtesy of Sam Cohn of the Baltimore Sun: "I would like for him to be able to have a day where [the Bengals] miss him. ... If it was me, I'd want to me them regret it."

Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson took it a step further, outright predicting a multi-sack game for Hendrickson, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN:

It's all pretty mild so far. It's also probably a little perplexing for Bengals fans considering the good years the club and Hendrickson had together. Those, before the weird split marked by weirder contract standoffs that seemed perfectly avoidable.

Alas, Hendrickson choosing to go to a rival in the AFC North and this revenge framing coming out of Baltimore won't exactly have Bengals fans feeling nostalgic on Sunday as they watch and hope he stays away from Joe Burrow.

articles.title: Lawson looks beyond Red Bull: 'If I can go to a team that gives me a better chance'
articles.summary: Liam Lawson has hinted that he could leave the Red Bull family after 2027 if an opportunity arises with a team capable of fighting for victories. The Racing...
articles.body:
Liam Lawson has hinted that he could leave the Red Bull family after 2027 if an opportunity arises with a team capable of fighting for victories. The Racing Bulls driver also acknowledged that Red Bull's decisions over its driver line-up have not always been based purely on performance.

The New Zealander is still waiting to find out whether he will retain his seat for next season. His future remains uncertain, with Formula 2 title contender Nikola Tsolov among the candidates for a promotion to Racing Bulls, while Arvid Lindblad is expected to remain with the team for a second season.

With limited opportunities elsewhere on the grid for 2027, Lawson discussed the possibility of leaving the Red Bull programme at the end of that season, when more seats could become available for 2028, speaking to GPblog and other media.

He did not rule it out. He framed the question around the ambition every driver on the grid shares.

I don't know if I have to do anything, but I think, for me personally, I mean, for all of us as drivers, our goal is to win. So for me, my focus is to put myself in a position where I can be winning for one, and if I can go to a team that gives me a better chance to do that, that's obviously what we're what we get to do.

Then he made a pointed comment about how his employer decides who drives: "The Red Bull specifics of it, I think they've shown many times in the past that sometimes that's not entirely why they make decisions, so it is something that I don't know what's going to happen next year, but for me, it's honestly not really what I'm thinking about now," Lawson said.

He added that a future elsewhere "has always been sort of talked about, and obviously you always try to cover your bases. But right now, not too much." For now, he said, his attention is on the final races and on Racing Bulls being "well in the fight for P5" in the constructors' championship.

A different tone from the Lawson of 2023

This marks a change in the way Lawson speaks about his future within the Red Bull family. Back in late 2023, after missing out on a race seat for the following season, the New Zealander made it clear that he saw Red Bull as his only route into Formula 1 : "I'm a Red Bull driver. If I ever get a chance in Formula 1, it'll be through Red Bull Racing ."

His career has taken several turns since then. Isack Hadjar's Red Bull contract has been extended through 2027 , leaving Lawson with little prospect of returning to the senior team in the immediate future. Racing Bulls therefore appears to be his only realistic option for remaining within the Red Bull organisation.

Why 2027 could be crucial for Lawson's F1 future

Securing another season at Racing Bulls would give Lawson the opportunity to strengthen his position on the grid and attract interest from teams outside the Red Bull family ahead of 2028, when more seats could become available.

For now, Lawson and Lindblad are considered the most likely pairing for Racing Bulls in 2027, with Tsolov potentially taking on a reserve role before being considered for a race seat the following year.

Such an arrangement would give Lawson another opportunity to prove himself, although it would not necessarily guarantee his long-term future with the team. With Tsolov waiting for his chance and Red Bull's senior seats seemingly unavailable, the New Zealander could eventually have to look elsewhere to continue his Formula 1 career.

articles.title: Hurricanes flip blue-chip linebacker Aston Whiteside from Aggies
articles.summary: The Miami Hurricanes flipped a blue-chip linebacker from an SEC program on Wednesday night. Four-star 2027 linebacker Aston Whiteside chnaged his commitment...
articles.body:
The Miami Hurricanes flipped a blue-chip linebacker from an SEC program on Wednesday night.

Four-star 2027 linebacker Aston Whiteside chnaged his commitment from Texas A&M to Miami, announcing his decision on social media.

Whiteside, who is listed at 6 foot 2 and 205 pounds, is ranked as the No. 27 linebacker and No. 347 player in the 2027 class, according to 247Sports' composite rankings.

Whiteside visited UM for its home game against Florida State this past weekend. Prior to the game, he told the South Florida Sun Sentinel he wanted to see a lot of "energy, physicality and competitiveness."

"It's a big rivalry game, so I want to see how the team responds to that atmosphere and competes for four quarters," Whiteside said.

Although Whiteside, a Burleson, Texas, native, committed to Texas A&M on June 1, he said Miami's staff kept trying to sway him.

"Miami has definitely continued to recruit me hard and show me a lot of love," Whiteside said last week.

Last season, Whiteside had 46 tackles, three tackles for loss and a forced fumble. This year, he has 91 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, four sacks and one forced fumble. He also has a punt return touchdown.

Whiteside, whose father played in the NFL and CFL, has a high GPA, and the Hurricanes like his maturity and intelligence in addition to his athleticism, a UM source said.

Whiteside joins two other blue-chip linebackers in the Hurricanes' 2027 class: A.J. Randle Jr. and Noah Glover.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs: I'm just trying to play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward
articles.summary: The Packers running back returned to the team this week after missing six games on the Commissioner's Exempt List.
articles.body:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs practiced Wednesday and has a chance to play Sunday.

Jacobs missed the first six games on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

He opened his first media session since his May 26 arrest with a statement.

"First, I'm excited to be back with the team, with the guys," Jacobs said, via video from Ryan Wood of USA Today. "I want to say thank you to the organization, really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. With that being said, I can't get into things, like specifics of things, but obviously, man, I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation. Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur, and four-second, three-second decisions can alter your life honestly. With that being said, man, still a human being, man. Still trying to learn. Still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this process, legally and just personally. Yeah, man, going forward, man, just trying to get better."

Jacobs remains under investigation by the NFL for Personal Conduct Policy violations stemming from his misdemeanor battery charge. On Sept. 10, he pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property.

He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property.

The original criminal complaint said surveillance video of the altercation shows at least part of the incident, but Jacobs and the victim filed suit to have the evidence permanently sealed. The NFL has left open the possibility of further punishment based on not being privy to exactly what's on the video.

Jacobs, though, was happy to be back with his teammates this week.

"I'm not trying to win nobody back, and that's just me being all the way honest because at the end of the day, like I said, I know what happened," Jacobs said. "And if you feel some type of way, obviously I feel bad because it's still a situation that occurred, and it should've never even happened. So that's something that I still will understand if people feel some type of way about it, but like I said, all I can do is keep showing up and being who I am, being a leader for this team, being a leader in this community and that's really all I can control."

The NFL placed Jacobs on paid leave Aug. 30, but he said he never doubted he would play again.

"I wasn't overly concerned about that, because in my heart I know what happened and what didn't happen, and I just trusted the legal process," Jacobs said. "For me, I was never overly concerned of not playing again. It was just a matter of time of when."

He also intimated that he disagrees with the league's decision to sit him for six games, which is the baseline punishment for domestic battery.

"I think six games was a lot, honestly, but that's not really up to me to decide," Jacobs said. "I'm grateful to be playing, so that's not even something I'm like arguing or petitioning with. I'm just happy to be back on the team."

Jacobs said he isn't concerned about how anyone outside the locker room feels about him after the May 23 incident with a woman at his home.

"I know for some people, this might be a stain on me and my character," Jacobs said. "I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lot of people that know me in this locker room or that have been around me, I'll let them do that. But for me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here and play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward."

But he also said the time away from the game gave him an opportunity to reevaluate his life.

"Obviously you never want to be in this situation," Jacobs said. "But just me being honest, it was probably one of the best things that's ever happened to me. It gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what's important and what I want my life to look like and what do I want people want to know me for. When they think of me, what [are] they going to say?"

articles.title: Aaron Boone stays, but what about the rest of the Yankees coaches?
articles.summary: Aaron Boone's status is settled. Here's what the Yankees must address with their coaching staff next.
articles.body:
NEW YORK – There's no promise beyond 2027, yet, but Aaron Boone retains the full trust and faith of Yankees ownership.

Hal Steinbrenner put "the majority of the responsibility'' for this year's playoff exit on "the position players and the inability to score on a consistent basis" and "not on the shoulders of Aaron Boone."

Along with Boone returning for a 10 th season as Yanks manager, the final guaranteed year of his contract, GM Brian Cashman has agreed to a new deal.

Steinbrenner hasn't discussed another contract extension with Boone, though "it's something I'd certainly consider," the owner said Wednesday.

Operating without a guarantee beyond '27 "doesn't bother me at all," said Boone. "My focus is only on looking toward next year" and another title run.

Hal Steinbrenner's take on Aaron Boone's 2026 season

In making the Boone decision, Steinbrenner said he asked himself: "Did he manage the team well this season? I think the answer is 'yes.'

"I'm not going to make a change just to make a change," said Steinbrenner, two weeks after his 93-win club was swept by the Rays in the AL Division Series.

"Some clubs made (managerial) changes and I guess they had their reasons," said Steinbrenner. "I don't think you can pin the season and the unacceptable end to it on Aaron."

Largely without Aaron Judge (rib fracture, calf strain) and Giancarlo Stanton (multiple calf strains) and despite injury list stretches by key veteran pitchers, Boone piloted a Yankee team to postseason for the eighth time in nine years.

But a second straight ALDS elimination versus a division foe, and a 17 th year without a world championship, has put further scrutiny on Yankees leadership.

Beyond the team's obvious talent, criticism about toughness and accountability are not unfair.

"I know I get accused sometimes of being too positive," Boone said of his public takes on player mistakes. "There is probably a time and place for that, but generally speaking, to me that's not leadership.

"That's me giving red meat to people who want to be upset with somebody," said Boone, preferring to address those issues one-to-one, or with the group.

"I know how hard it is to walk out there every single day in a game of failure."

Yankees vs. Rays ALDS Game 3 photos from Yankee Stadium

But the club's defensive issues in ALDS Game 2 and lapses in judgment by certain players didn't reflect well on the manager and his staff.

Several of Boone's coaches, including pitching coach Matt Blake and catching coordinator Tanner Swanson – two key staffers – are on expiring contracts.

A full staff evaluation has yet to occur, with scrutiny falling mostly on batting coach James Rowson and his assistants.

"I think James leads a great hitting group," said Boone. "I've been really impressed with the culture he's created…over the last few seasons."

Aaron Boone: 'I believe it can happen with me'

Moving into an 18th year since the Yanks' last world championship, Boone said, "I believe it can happen with me at the helm.

"But any answer I give in defense of that isn't going to be a great one or satisfy people."

Boone had no specific regrets about 2026, though he alluded to "conversations you have with guys throughout the year that, could you have gotten more out of this guy?"

Once more, Boone "certainly felt like we had a team capable of making a deep run," but was eliminated by the eventual AL East champ for a second straight year.

"I'd say every year is hard," said Boone. "This feels up there as one of the hardest."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start ‘Em, Sit ‘Em Week 7: Kyler Murray, Woody Marks, Ashton Jeanty, Tucker Kraft, and More
articles.summary: Injuries and bye weeks are making fantasy football lineup decisions increasingly difficult. We also have enough information six weeks into the season to know...
articles.body:
Injuries and bye weeks are making fantasy football lineup decisions increasingly difficult. We also have enough information six weeks into the season to know which roles are real, which performances were fluky, and which matchups should materially change how we view a player.

That's especially important with start/sit decisions. I'm not here to tell you to start obvious superstars. The useful calls come further down the rankings, where two players may look similar on the surface but usage, opponent tendencies, or expected game script can provide a meaningful reason to prefer one over the other.

A "sit" also doesn't always mean a player absolutely belongs on your bench. Running back is thin enough that managers may have no realistic alternative to someone such as Ashton Jeanty. In those cases, the designation is more about lowering expectations and understanding where the risk comes from.

Here are my favorite fantasy football starts and sits for Week 7.

Start Kyler Murray, QB, Minnesota Vikings

The Minnesota Vikings were on bye last week, and those players can occasionally get overlooked when managers scan the previous week's box scores before making waiver claims. Kyler Murray was available in one of my leagues where I needed a replacement for Trevor Lawrence, and I was able to add him without anyone else even bidding.

I like Murray quite a bit against the Indianapolis Colts. He scored 18.26 fantasy points against the New Orleans Saints in Week 5, and the Colts are allowing 18.4 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks. That isn't an overwhelmingly favorable matchup, but it is good enough when paired with Murray's improving rushing usage.

Murray has 84 rushing yards over his past three games. He ran 10 times for 51 yards against New Orleans before the bye, and those rushing points give him a path to a useful fantasy day even if Minnesota doesn't need him to pile up passing attempts.

The primary concern is volume. Indianapolis may not put enough pressure on the Vikings to create a back-and-forth game, and Minnesota could conceivably score three or four touchdowns without Murray accounting for all of them. Still, the combination of matchup and rushing upside puts him firmly in streaming territory for me.

Sit Tyler Shough, QB, New Orleans Saints

Tyler Shough scored roughly 27 fantasy points last week, but the way he got there is exactly why I'm fading him in Week 7.

Shough threw for only 144 yards. He somehow turned that into three passing touchdowns, then added 32 rushing yards and another touchdown on the ground. All four scores counted, of course, but touchdown production like that doesn't correlate well with such limited yardage. It was an extremely efficient fantasy result that I don't view as sustainable.

We saw the downside one week earlier when Shough threw for only 96 scoreless yards against the Vikings. The Saints also have one of the weakest running games in football, which puts even more responsibility on Shough when the offense runs into a difficult matchup.

Pittsburgh qualifies. The Steelers are allowing just 11.9 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks, the fourth-fewest in the league. Their pass rush can also make life difficult for a quarterback who hasn't consistently handled pressure well.

I expect the entire New Orleans offense to have trouble moving the ball, particularly with this game being played overseas. Shough may have to throw enough to accumulate some volume, but I'm not chasing the four-touchdown box score from last week.

Matchup matters a great deal to me when we're choosing among non-elite quarterbacks. Aaron Rodgers, for example, has scored at least 17 fantasy points in four consecutive games and multiple touchdowns in four straight. I'd rather look for a streamer in a better situation than force Shough into my lineup.

Woody Marks was my sit at running back last week. He is now my favorite start at the position for Week 7.

The reason for the reversal is simple: My concern last week was Jacksonville's run defense, not Marks' role. He still managed 10.1 PPR points on 15 carries for 56 yards and two receptions for 25 yards. More importantly, the underlying usage was exactly what fantasy managers wanted to see.

Marks played 78% of Houston's offensive snaps and ran a route on 60% of C.J. Stroud's dropbacks. Those are lead-back numbers, not committee numbers. Jawhar Jordan will spell him for a drive here and there, but Marks handled 18 of Houston's 25 running back opportunities last week.

Jordan also happened to score Houston's only rushing touchdown on a long run. I don't view that as evidence that Marks lost the valuable carries. Marks had already been Houston's goal-line back when David Montgomery was active, and I expect him to get opportunities near the end zone if the Texans reach that area against the New York Giants.

The matchup is much more favorable this time around. The Giants are allowing the 15th-most fantasy points per game to running backs, and Houston should have a positive game script. Marks has seen 15 carries in back-to-back games, with a strong receiving role attached to that workload.

Sit Ashton Jeanty, RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Most managers cannot actually bench Ashton Jeanty, so think of this as a warning rather than an instruction to sit him for any running back you can find.

I continue to be unimpressed by his rushing performance. Jeanty is averaging only 3.2 yards per carry and hasn't reached 60 rushing yards in a game since Week 1. He has also been held to exactly 10 carries in back-to-back games.

The usage trend is becoming a concern. Jeanty handled only 50% of the Raiders' rushing attempts last week, when Mike Washington Jr. had nine carries to Jeanty's 10. Jeanty turned those 10 attempts into just 22 yards against a Buffalo defense that entered the game as a favorable rushing matchup.

His receiving work has covered up much of that inefficiency. Jeanty is averaging 10.5 fantasy points per game from his receiving production alone. In PPR formats, several catches can rescue an otherwise poor rushing day, and that's largely why he remains difficult to bench.

Los Angeles does allow a 19.5% target share to running backs, the eighth-highest rate in the league, so there is certainly a path for Jeanty to accumulate receptions again. The problem is that the Rams are allowing the 12th-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs overall and only 93 rushing yards per game to the position.

Jeanty can PPR scam his way to another acceptable fantasy score. I just don't want managers looking at the name or draft capital and assuming the underlying rushing role is still elite. The carry share is moving in the wrong direction, and Washington is closer to an even split than most managers want to acknowledge.

Start Denzel Boston, WR, Cleveland Browns

Denzel Boston caught one pass for 15 yards last week, which creates exactly the type of situation where fantasy managers start wondering whether they should take a productive player out of the lineup.

I'm going back to him against Tennessee.

Boston has played 92% of Cleveland's offensive snaps this season. That is elite playing-time security for any receiver, much less a rookie. He has also produced 1.82 yards per route run, a strong number given the quarterback environment he's been working in.

The Tennessee Titans are allowing the eighth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers. Boston's role gives him the opportunity to benefit from that matchup, and his downfield ability gives him a higher ceiling than several receivers in this range who rely on short receptions.

I have Boston as a top-30 receiver this week. Last week's one-catch performance doesn't change that.

Omar Cooper Jr. returned from injured reserve and immediately gave fantasy managers plenty to get excited about. He ran a route on 79% of Geno Smith's dropbacks and earned a 24% target share, which is an excellent first-game role for a rookie coming off an extended absence.

The production followed. Cooper went over 100 receiving yards and scored a touchdown, showing why he deserves to be rostered and why there is real rest-of-season upside here.

I don't want to chase those points against Miami, though. Part of Cooper's Week 6 production came on a long touchdown created by busted coverage. Take away that one play, and the box score would have looked much less likely to force him immediately into fantasy lineups.

The Miami Dolphins are allowing the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers. That sounds strange because their defense hasn't been particularly imposing, but game script matters. Teams have frequently gotten ahead of Miami and no longer needed to throw enough for opposing receivers to pile up fantasy production.

Aaron Glenn wants to run the football when the Jets can control the game. Whether Breece Hall is available or the carries go elsewhere, the larger point is the same: If New York gets ahead, passing volume could disappear quickly.

Cooper's Week 6 usage is a very good reason to hold him. It isn't enough for me to ignore the Week 7 environment and chase last week's fantasy total.

Start Tucker Kraft, TE, Green Bay Packers

Tucker Kraft hasn't had the breakout season I expected, but there may not be a better spot for him to finally produce a ceiling game.

The biggest issue has been Green Bay's receiving hierarchy. I expected Christian Watson to function as the Packers' No. 1 receiving option with Kraft second. Instead, Matthew Golden has emerged and pushed Kraft closer to third. For tight ends, there is a meaningful fantasy difference between being the second option in a passing game and being the third.

Kraft is still playing enough. His snap share is around 80%, so this isn't a case where he's disappearing from the offense. He has simply scored one touchdown all season and hasn't had the spike game I expected.

Detroit provides about as good a chance as possible for that to change. The Lions are allowing 31.9 fantasy points per game to tight ends. That's more than 10 points per game above the next-worst defense against the position.

That is an absurd gap six weeks into the season, and this game also has the potential to turn into one of the highest-scoring matchups on the slate. Kraft doesn't need to suddenly become the Packers' No. 2 target for me to like him here. He just needs his normal playing time in a matchup that has been historically favorable to tight ends so far.

I think Kraft scores this week, and I have him ranked as one of my top tight ends for Week 7.

AJ Barner is the deeper option for managers who don't have the luxury of starting someone such as Kraft.

There is almost nothing exciting about Barner's season-long fantasy production. He has scored five points or fewer in all but two games and has only one game with more than 20 receiving yards. If we were looking strictly at his previous box scores, there would be no reason to start him.

His role is better than those numbers suggest. Barner has played 89% of Seattle's offensive snaps this season, so he is consistently on the field and available to run routes. The missing piece has been targets.

Kansas City gives us a reason to believe those targets could arrive this week. The Chiefs are allowing the fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers but the third-most to tight ends. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is still going to get his opportunities, but Seattle doesn't have a second wide receiver who has established himself as a consistent target earner.

That creates a scenario where Barner can become the No. 2 option in the passing game for a week. There's plenty of risk given what he's done so far, but managers searching for a waiver-wire tight end usually aren't choosing among safe players.

If I'm down bad at the position because of injuries or bye weeks, Barner is one of the streamers I'm willing to use.

Sit Michael Mayer, TE, Las Vegas Raiders

Michael Mayer is finally relevant enough that calling him a sit actually matters.

Brock Bowers may technically play tight end, but functionally he is the Raiders' No. 1 receiver. Mayer is still occupying the traditional tight end role, and he has produced TE1-level fantasy numbers in two of his past three games.

The problem is what happened in the other game. Mayer has alternated useful performances with complete duds, including a game in that stretch where he barely cleared one fantasy point. That volatility is difficult to embrace when the matchup also works against him.

The Rams are allowing just 8.3 fantasy points per game to tight ends, the second-fewest in the league according to the matchup data I'm using this week. They have been excellent against the pass overall, which lowers my expectations for the entire Raiders passing game.

Mayer's role gives him a reasonable chance to see targets, but I'm not seeing much ceiling in this particular spot. A line around two catches for 20 yards is very much in play if the Raiders struggle to sustain drives.

If you have to use Mayer because the position is thin, that's understandable. If I have another legitimate option, though, this is a week where I'm looking elsewhere.

articles.title: What I’m hearing at Gillette Stadium: Wednesday word (Week 7)
articles.summary: The Patriots held one final practice before leaving for Chicago ahead of their primetime matchup.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass — The buses have departed Gillette Stadium, and the New England Patriots are on their way to Chicago for a primetime matchup against the Bears.

But before they left, they held one final practice.

Given the injury scare that Week 6's win over the New York Jets brought, the New England Patriots got good news as the short week progressed. And on Friday, only two players were absent from the media-attended portion of practice: G Alijah Vera-Tucker and G Ben Brown. Those two were expected, with Vrabel revealing that it was unlikely the two would be ready to go in such a quick turnaround. However, Morgan Moses has been a limited participant after leaving the game early with an ankle injury, and cornerback Carlton Davis practiced for the second straight day on Wednesday after having been sidelined with a neck injury.

After practice, head coach Mike Vrabel provided updates and injury designations for key players. Brown (knee) and Vera-Tucker (hamstring) have been ruled out, as well as cornerbacks Karon Prunty (hamstring), Channing Canada (hamstring), and Carlton Davis (neck).

The Patriots also have the option to activate tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve, but Vrabel wouldn't commit to whether they would or not, emphasizing they "have until 3:00 p.m. Central Time."

As for who is questionable, the Patriots have S Kevin Byard III (chest), LB Christian Elliss (chest), T Morgan Moses (foot), and S Craig Woodson (shoulder).

With Brown and Vera-Tucker out, it will be Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse who are set to start after having stepped in on Sunday's game.

"I felt great," Pryor told Patriots Wire. "The coaches did a great job of having the game plan ready, and I'm just ready to go out there and play with the guys."

For Pryor, he emphasized that the opportunity in the Week 6 game provided him with extra confidence as he didn't get the opportunity to get "the extra reps during camp and OTAs."

"Had me lacking a bit," he said. "But they did a great job of bringing me up to speed, and obviously the reps over the past two weeks have helped as well."

Plus, it definitely helped that the offensive line did not give up a sack in last week's game despite being down three linemen.

"Execution fuels motion, and it's been harped on," he said. "That phrase has been with me since my rookie year, and it just fuels us going into the next week. So I'm very excited to get out there and see what the rest of us can do this week."

Rhamondre Stevenson emphasizes importance of the run game against Chicago

The run game is going to be very important against the Bears in this primetime game, and Rhamondre Stevenson is excited for the challenge.

"They've got a good run defense. They've got a good defense, period," Stevenson told Patriots Wire. "But it just comes down to staying on track, trusting our linemen. Me, TreVeyon, and Corey- just trusting the linemen, just getting downhill, trying to get positive plays. No negative runs in the run game."

While the Patriots are dealing with offensive line injuries, last week's final drive with Corey Kiner inspired a lot of confidence, and Stevenson has faith in each of the guys that step on the field.

"Those guys work super hard," he added. "No matter where they're at on the depth chart, I feel like they all come and are learning the same things, hearing the same calls, and really taking a growing approach to try to do things the right way. So very confident."

Cornerback Charles Woods has stepped up a lot over these last few weeks, and one humorous moment at halftime has earned him a new nickname.

Woods asked his head coach if he was allowed to have a Jolly Rancher, which Vrabel found hilarious, and he gave him one. And next thing he knew, Woods recorded his first interception of his NFL career. So now, Vrabel makes sure to always keep grape ones on him, as it's the cornerback's favorite flavor.

"I kind of like him. He got a little street rat in him," Vrabel said. "The story was, he was like, 'coach, can I get a Jolly Rancher?' And I was like, 'Are you serious?' I'm like, 'yes.' At halftime, it was like I was coaching one of the kids teams, 9-year-old football. 'Yeah, sure have a Jolly Rancher.'

"Then we won the game. And then I joked about it when he got a game ball, we called him Jolly Rancher or JR now for short. So then last week I said, 'I'm ready to go. I got your grape Jolly Rancher.' Put one in and the next play he got an interception. I was like, 'This is crazy.'"

So, does he have some ready for Chicago?

"I've got them packed, ready to go," Vrabel said.

Eli Raridon's confidence continues to grow

It's been six weeks of experience for Eli Raridon, and the rookie tight end's confidence is continuing to grow with each snap.

"I'm just trying to improve every week and just get better and more acclimated to the offense and just playing these snaps in this league has helped me gain confidence and be more comfortable for sure," he told Patriots Wire. "I'm a pretty big critic of myself, and my coaches are also doing the same, and we're just trying to improve in every aspect."

Plus, the Patriots are down a few wide receivers due to injury, so that makes their ability to catch the ball along with blocking even more important.

"That's what we take pride in, doing both things," he said. "Hunter's a great example of doing that and that's something that we have to be doing."

Vrabel on Bears' returner Kalif Raymond: "I got a lot of affinity for Kalif Raymond. He helped us win a lot of games at Tennessee. He's a great teammate. Probably one of the toughest, smaller-bodied players in the league, and I mean that with a lot of sincerity. He's willing to block, he's got great courage, he runs through the smoke as a returner. He did a lot of different jobs for us, and he's continued to do a lot of those jobs with the Lions and now the Bears. He's just a valuable piece for them. You can put him in a lot of different places."

Stevenson on playing at Soldier Field: "It was a great environment. A lot of history in that stadium. So, excited to play there again."

DeMario Douglas on A.J. Brown getting another opportunity on the field: "I can't wait. I can't wait. I know it's due."

Dre'Mont Jones on the Bears' rushing attack: "Creativity and volume are definitely keys, but I think a lot of it, about 75% of it, is probably the quarterback."

Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook .

articles.title: Lions’ Sam Laporta drops NSFW ‘disappointing’ admission about not getting contract extension
articles.summary: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta is frustrated with his contract situation, and he made it clear that he believes his contributions to the team deserve mo...
articles.body:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta is frustrated with his contract situation, and he made it clear that he believes his contributions to the team deserve more recognition.

LaPorta expressed disappointment that the Lions have yet to offer him a contract extension. The tight end is approaching free agency at the end of the season and could be playing elsewhere next year if Detroit does not get a deal done.

"It's disappointing that you go out there every week and bear the risk of getting hurt," LaPorta told Pardon My Take (Via Jordan Schultz). "Like last year, I broke my f—ing back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

LaPorta's comments show the frustration of a player who believes he has done everything asked of him while waiting for the team to reward his performance. His reference to "breaking his back" underscores the physical toll of playing in the NFL and the risk players accept every time they step onto the field.

Despite his disappointment, LaPorta made it clear that he intends to keep producing for Detroit. However, he also acknowledged that his future might not include the Lions if the two sides cannot agree on an extension.

"I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good," LaPorta said. "I'll go get paid somewhere else. So whatever."

That is a blunt message from a player who would seemingly prefer to remain in Detroit but is not prepared to wait indefinitely for a new deal.

If Sam LaPorta reaches the open market, his receiving ability and experience with the Lions could make him an attractive option for teams looking to upgrade at tight end . His contract situation will be worth monitoring as the offseason approaches, particularly if Detroit allows negotiations to continue without an agreement.

articles.title: Rams haven’t talked about bringing in a WR with Davante Adams out
articles.summary: Sean McVay told reporters that the Rams haven’t talked about trading for or signing a wide receiver with Davante Adams injured.
articles.body:
Earlier this week, the Los Angeles Rams learned that star wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring in the team's 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Adams will be out for six to 10 weeks, as he has to undergo surgery. The team has already placed him on injured reserve.

Even with Adams' extended absence, paired with Terrance Ferguson's stint on IR, the team isn't ready for a new face. Sean McVay told reporters that the Rams haven't had any discussions about bringing in a new receiver.

The Rams did trade for Tutu Atwell before the season; thus, the team currently has six wide receivers on its active roster. Atwell is joined by Puka Nacua, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Alex Bachman, and rookie CJ Daniels. The Rams also have four tight ends active.

Mumpfield played extensive snaps when Nacua missed two games earlier this season, having a career night against the Denver Broncos with four catches for 93 yards and one touchdown. Perhaps that's playing into the reason why the Rams aren't seeking a trade yet.

articles.title: Texans savor Tank Dell’s emotional return after a catastrophic knee injury
articles.summary: HOUSTON (AP) — Tank Dell will play his first game in nearly two years on Sunday and the Houston Texans are thrilled that their receiver is back after a catas...
articles.body:
HOUSTON (AP) — Tank Dell will play his first game in nearly two years on Sunday and the Houston Texans are thrilled that their receiver is back after a catastrophic knee injury.

Coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that they aren't putting any expectations on Dell's performance against the New York Giants after he was out for so long and that it will just be exciting to see him back on the field.

"The main thing is him just going out playing ball," Ryans said. "I don't care how many reps he gets, but I'll have my Tank Dell jersey on on Sunday."

Defensive end Will Anderson Jr. shared that enthusiasm when talking about Dell's return.

"I've been hugging Tank all day," Anderson said. "I haven't left his side all day. ... I was telling him, every time I saw him today, I said bro: 'I'm so proud of you, man.'"

Dell missed all last season and the first six games this season recovering from a dislocated knee and multiple torn knee ligaments he sustained on Dec. 21, 2024. He had 51 receptions for 667 yards and three scores before his injury in what was his second NFL season.

He has a lot of emotions as his return approaches after many long and tough months filled with hard work and rehabilitation.

"I'm anxious, of course, it's been two years, well (almost) two years since I've played," he said. "But I don't think I'm overwhelmed, I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football. I'm blessed, man."

And he's envisioned what it will be like when he makes that long-awaited first grab.

"I don't care if the first catch is 2 yards, I'm spiking the ball," he said half-jokingly. "And it's going to feel good. I know there's a lot of questions like how's he going to look when he gets tackled? I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. ... y'all are going to see the passion I have after I have that first catch."

His most recent injury wasn't the only one Dell has dealt with since the Texans drafted him in the third round in 2023 following a standout career at the University of Houston. His rookie season, where he scored seven touchdowns, was cut short when he broke his leg in Week 13.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud, who counts Dell among his closest friends, saw everything he did behind the scenes to get to this point and raved about how he approached the entire process.

"The main thing is he always had a smile on his face, even probably when he wasn't feeling like smiling," Stroud said. "His attitude through the whole process has been great."

Dell returns to a crowded receiver room that recently added star Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. He isn't worried about getting his touches and is simply excited to contribute to the talented group.

While Dell can't wait to play on Sunday, there is one drawback to his return. So many people want to come to the game to support him that it's costing him a pretty penny.

"I had to buy so many extra tickets, I'm kinda upset about that," he said with a laugh. "But I'm happy because they were with me through this whole journey."

A very special guest will be his grandmother whom he paid to fly from Florida to be at Reliant Stadium on Sunday.

After playing collegiately in town and making so many electric plays in his first two seasons with the team, Dell is undoubtedly a favorite among Texans fans.

And he can't wait to see how they respond to him on Sunday.

"I feel like they're going to go crazy," he said. "I'm excited for that."

articles.title: Ohio State Can – And Will – Make College Football Playoff Despite Injury
articles.summary: Ohio State has enough talent around any quarterback to still contend for the national championship. Ohio State football is bigger […]
articles.body:
Ohio State has enough talent around any quarterback to still contend for the national championship.

Ohio State football is bigger than one player.

That being said, the Buckeyes are going to need to adjust in the wake of losing starting quarterback Julian Sayin.

Sayin was a perfect option at the position. He possesses a strong arm, a good understanding of the offense and a knack for finding Jeremiah Smith.

Ryan Day, the head coach for the Buckeyes, informed the media that Sayin will be lost through the postseason. The burden of leading Ohio State now falls onto the shoulders of Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair.

Sayin, a Heisman Trophy finalist a year ago, was injured in a big win over defending national champion Indiana this past Saturday. He has completed over 71 percent of his passes this year, throwing for almost 1,800 yards and 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions.

Luke Fahey Likely Gets The First Crack At Replacing Julian Sayin

In terms of experience, Fahey is ahead of St. Clair.

The freshman from California has thrown 13 passes this year, completing nine for 203 yards and two touchdowns. He was the one Day went to when Sayin went down vs. Indiana.

Despite not completing either of his pass attempts, he also did nothing wrong. The Buckeyes survived, and now, thanks to being on a bye, have ample time to prepare him for USC.

St. Clair, a sophomore from Ohio, is 5-for-9 in his career, including all five completions this season for 52 yards and a touchdown.

Whether Fahey Or St. Clair, Jeremiah Smith Will Be The Key

No matter if it is Fahey or St. Clair that Ohio State's coaching staff decides on, or both for that matter, getting the ball to Smith is the key.

The Heisman frontrunner, Smith is a difference maker on the field.

The junior has caught 52 passes for 984 yards, scoring 12 touchdowns. He is tied for the NCAA lead in receptions, second in yards and second in touchdowns.

Smith went over 200 receiving yards with six total touchdowns in wins over Illinois and Iowa, settling for 93 vs. Maryland and 68 vs. Indiana. But his touchdown catch vs. the Hoosiers changed the momentum of the contest.

Look for the Buckeyes to find ways to get Smith the ball outside of just deep throws. That will keep Fahey or St. Clair from feeling the pressure that comes with being QB1 at The Ohio State University.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown reacts to his Sixers debut after road win over Knicks
articles.summary: Star forward Jaylen Brown reacts to his Philadelphia 76ers debut after a road win over the New York Knicks to open the season.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia 76ers saw the debuts of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown in their impressive 106-100 road win over the New York Knicks on Tuesday. The Sixers spoiled ring night for the defending champs and they were able to make a statement in the early going of the season.

Brown finished with 19 points on 7-for-14 shooting, knocked down two triples, and had eight rebounds and six assists. He was a plus-17 in the 35 minutes he played (take that analytics people) and he was a big part of Philadelphia's defensive unit in the second half.

It's game 1 of 82, but Brown is happy with what he and the Sixers were able to accomplish on opening night.

"Just trying to win as many games as possible, stack days, and I think it's still early for us," Brown said after the win. "We're still figuring out a lot of stuff, so we still have a lot to learn and grow, but it's good to learn and grow and win at the same time."

Things were understandably clunky for the Sixers at times on Tuesday. There were moments where players didn't know exactly where they needed to be and there were some tough turnovers, but the Sixers buckled down when they needed to. The execution was much better after halftime, and great in the fourth quarter to close this game out and open the season on a high note. Work to do, for sure, but a good start.

"I think it was just OK," Brown said of the team's chemistry. "We got a lot of room for growth, room for improvement. So I'm looking forward to building with my teammates, but it's always good when you can win and learn at the same time."

Brown, a very high IQ basketball player, understands the talent on this team. The Sixers are going to win a lot of games just because of the presence of himself, James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and VJ Edgecombe as well as a strong supporting cast. Now, the goal and focus is to build that cohesion.

"I think we're just figuring it out," Brown finished. "We're not even at the tip of the iceberg in terms of hitting chemistry, understanding yourself on the floor, understanding our spacing. We're still at the very early stages of what we could possibly be. So it's a good sign that we can win while still being at that early stage."

The Sixers will host the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday in the home opener.

articles.title: When Dalton Rushing can return to full-time catching for the Dodgers after elbow surgery
articles.summary: When news broke that Dalton Rushing suffered a partially torn UCL in his right elbow back in August, fans openly wondered if and when the Los Angeles Dodgers...
articles.body:
When news broke that Dalton Rushing suffered a partially torn UCL in his right elbow back in August, fans openly wondered if and when the Los Angeles Dodgers catcher would have surgery to fix it.

At the time, any surgery would have effectively ended his season, leaving LA without a key bat on the bench, so, after deliberation, the team opted for rehab instead, allowing Rushing to remain a pinch-hitting option for another World Series run.

Unfortunately, that World Series berth didn't materialize, and now Rushing will be unable to catch full-time for the next nine months after undergoing right elbow surgery on October 21, which Andrew Freedman revealed to reporters like Maddie Lee of the LA Times during his season-of-season press conference.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Dodgers' Dalton Rushing is undergoing right elbow surgery today, per sources," Lee wrote. "It's expected to be a hybrid internal brace procedure. The expected timeline to return to catching full time is 9 months, with a return to hitting well before then."

On paper, the Dodgers' desire to keep Rushing's bat available made sense, as he was a quality performer at times during the season. But the emergence of Josue De Paula as a major league hitter quickly made Rushing irrelevant, to the point where he didn't take a single at-bat against the Atlanta Braves or the Milwaukee Brewers. With his catching return now set for mid-summer, the Dodgers will have to hope reserves like Hunter Feduccia can hold things down behind Will Smith, or that Rushing can find some work at first base to remain a more consistent part of Dave Roberts' offense.

articles.title: Brady Tkachuk Trolled By Senators Fans in Return After Panthers Trade in Trending Videos
articles.summary: Florida Panthers left wing Brady Tkachuck made his return to Ottawa, where he played the first eight seasons of his NHL career before being traded last June, on Wednesday evening.
articles.body:
Florida Panthers left wing Brady Tkachuck made his return to Ottawa, where he played the first eight seasons of his NHL career before being traded last June, on Wednesday evening.

Needless to say, Senators fans were ready and waiting for Tkachuk, who told Ottawa he would not re-sign at the end of his current deal, eventually leading to the trade that united him with his older brother, Matthew.

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 🔮

As one can imagine, the fans weren't happy when Tkachuk scored the game's first goal.

Tkachuk was a superstar in Ottawa, making the All-Star Game on four occasions and scoring 463 points (213 goals, 250 assists). The Senators also fared well in the past two seasons after missing the playoffs for seven straight campaigns, winning 89 combined games. Tkachuk, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2018 NHL draft, also served as the team's captain for the past five seasons.

The 27-year-old is playing on a seven-year, $57.5 million contract that runs through the 2027-28 season. However, he made it clear that he wasn't re-signing with Ottawa, leading to the trade.

The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported that four teams (the Panthers, Vegas Golden Knights, Minnesota Wild and Carolina Hurricanes) were on the list for Tkachuk, who has a no-movement clause.

"There's professional reasons, personal reasons why I wasn't going to re-sign here," Tkachuk told reporters on Wednesday, per TSN .

"A lot of those things remain private between [general manager Steve Staios] and that's going to remain private. It just happened to work out this way," he said.

He also denied Senators owner Michael Andlauer's implication from September that Keith Tkachuk (Brady's father and a former NHL star) and Matthew had involvement in the deal.

"I saw the quote, and I mean he's entitled to his opinion. But I know for myself, it was 100 per cent my decision. [I'm a] big boy, I can make decisions for myself and my family. I don't need to be influenced by other people to make decisions. So he's entitled to his opinion," Tkachuk said.

Both teams have now moved on, although it's clear Senator fans (understandably) have not.

articles.title: Will Tiger Woods play in the Hero World Challenge? Health concerns cloud his December return
articles.summary: Tiger Woods has another chance to return to competitive golf, but his participation in the 2026 Hero World Challenge remains uncertain.
articles.body: Tiger Woods has another chance to return to competitive golf, but his participation in the 2026 Hero World Challenge remains uncertain. The tournament, which he hosts in the Bahamas, will run from December 3 to 6 and feature seven of the world's top 10 golfers. Woods is not among the 17 players announced so far, yet three exemption spots remain open. That leaves the door ajar for the 15-time major champion if his recovery allows him to compete. After a long stretch away from professional golf, even a small sign of progress has drawn attention to his possible comeback.Tiger Woods' Hero World Challenge comeback depends on his healthWoods has not competed in a professional tournament since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship. Since then, his recovery has been marked by several serious setbacks. He ruptured his Achilles tendon in March 2025 and underwent disc replacement surgery in October that year.He returned to action for one TGL match in March 2026, but a rollover car crash days later interrupted any momentum. Woods was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence and later pleaded no contest to a reduced reckless driving charge. He also announced that he would step away to seek treatment and focus on his health.There is still no confirmed date for his return. However, recent activity has renewed interest in his plans. Woods was listed on the roster for the third season of TGL, where he is set to captain Jupiter Links Golf Club. He was also seen hitting balls during a junior clinic at Pebble Beach last week.Those appearances offer signs of activity, but they do not confirm that he is ready for tournament golf. Woods has previously used a tournament exemption to enter his own Hero World Challenge, so one of the remaining spots could provide a route back if he feels prepared.Hero World Challenge 2026 field includes Scottie SchefflerThe confirmed field already features several major names. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler will lead the group, alongside Matt Fitzpatrick and Cameron Young. Chris Gotterup, Russell Henley, Xander Schauffele and Sam Burns are also among the players announced.Other confirmed competitors include J.J. Spaun, Si Woo Kim, Hideki Matsuyama, Justin Thomas, Tom Kim and Akshay Bhatia. Three tournament exemptions remain unfilled.If Woods returns, he is likely to follow a limited schedule rather than attempt a full season. In 2024, he played the four major championships and the Genesis Invitational, where he serves as tournament host. Now eligible for the Champions Tour at age 50, he also has another possible option.The Hero World Challenge could offer a relatively manageable setting for Woods to test his game. articles.title: Sexual offence charge rocks India's Asian Para Games contingent; swimmer faces lifetime ban
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya has been left embarrassed after para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya has been left embarrassed after para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident, and faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI).A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as “reprehensible and intolerable” and saying there could be “no justification” for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage.”“Aalam is staring at no less than a lifetime ban for bringing disrepute to the entire Indian delegation participating at the Asian Para Games and for embarrassing the country on the world stage,” the official said.According to the official, the incident occurred on Monday at the Four Points by Sheraton hotel, where the Indian para swimming team was staying. The female employee was reportedly carrying out housekeeping duties in the swimmer’s room when the alleged misconduct took place.“The local organising committee (LOC) informed the chef-de-mission’s (CDM) office that an alleged sexual harassment and molestation incident had occurred at the hotel and that an Indian athlete had been detained by the local police,” the official said.“When we reached the hotel, the police and senior hotel managers were already there. We were told that the athlete had inappropriately touched the female housekeeping staff member, made sexually coloured gestures, attempted to grope her and made sexual advances. She rushed out and informed her superiors. This is what we were told by the police and hotel staff,” the official added.The official said the delegation apologised to the hotel authorities and the employee. Following the complaint, police detained Shaikh and took him to a local police station. The official said the authorities sought his arrest and that he be formally presented before a court.The LOC subsequently intervened, with the Indian delegation asked to furnish a written apology to the employee and ensure that the athlete left Japan. Shaikh was moved to another hotel for the night and booked on the first available flight, departing Nagoya at around 2 pm local time on Tuesday, the official said. He was released after the written apology was furnished, according to the official’s account.“The police authorities had clearly recorded the sexual offence allegation in their formal complaint, in Japanese. We can confirm that since I saw that,” the official said.The official added the incident had diverted senior Indian officials from the contingent’s ongoing sporting campaign. “Instead of focusing on the Games and our athletes’ performances, we spent several hours at the police station and later at the hotel premises convincing the authorities. We were embarrassed in front of everyone,” the official said.He added that the employee appeared to be in deep shock when the delegation returned to the hotel. The hotel and LOC, he said, sought updates on the action India would take and warned that they could pursue formal legal proceedings if they were dissatisfied with the response.The PCI has informed the govt in New Delhi of the proposed action, the official said. articles.title: Wayne Gretzky bought a Florida mansion from son-in-law Dustin Johnson for $4.5 million in 2022; four years later, he sold it for $6.42 million
articles.summary: Wayne Gretzky and his wife, Janet, sold their Harbour Isles waterfront home in Florida on June 1, 2026, for $6.42 million.
articles.body: Wayne Gretzky and his wife, Janet, sold their Harbour Isles waterfront home in Florida on June 1, 2026, for $6.42 million. Gretzky had bought the 7,169-square-foot house from his son-in-law, golfer Dustin Johnson, for $4.5 million in 2022. That is a gain of roughly $1.9 million on paper. The road there was rougher than the number suggests. The home first listed at $8.99 million in November 2025, dropped to $7.8 million, and still closed more than $1 million below that.How Gretzky made about $1.9 million on a house he bought from Dustin JohnsonThe purchase happened in March 2022. It was an off-market deal, which means the house never went through a public listing. Gretzky paid $4.5 million, or about $628 per square foot. When the home sold this year, the price worked out to roughly $895 per square foot. That is an increase of about 43 percent in four years.The longer view is just as interesting. Records show the house last sold in 2016 for $2.9 million. So in a decade it went from $2.9 million to $6.42 million, more than double. The home sits on 0.34 acres, and the building has stayed the same size throughout. What changed was South Florida. Palm Beach County's waterfront market ran hot for years, and Gretzky owned the house through most of that run.One caution on the "gain." It is the gap between two sale prices, not profit. Commissions, closing costs, taxes, insurance and upkeep on a large waterfront property all take a bite. The final take-home figure is lower, though no one outside the family knows by how much.Why the asking price fell by $2.57 millionLook at the November 2025 asking price again. At $8.99 million, the Gretzkys wanted almost exactly double what they paid. That is a bold opening bid, even in a strong market. Sellers of high-end homes often start high to leave room to negotiate, and sometimes it works. Here, it didn't.The price came down to $7.8 million, then the final deal landed at $6.42 million. That is $1.38 million under the last asking price, or nearly 18 percent. Measured against the first ask, the total drop was about 29 percent.Buyers in this price range tend to know what comparable homes are fetching. A house at $895 per square foot has to compete with every other waterfront option in the area. One example is a four-bedroom home down the same street, 788 Harbour Isles Place. It was listed in August 2026 at $5.595 million, or about $1,192 per square foot, for a smaller house of 4,693 square feet. That asking price had not been tested by a sale at the time of writing, so it proves little on its own. Still, it shows how widely prices vary inside one small community.What the Harbour Isles address gets a buyerHarbour Isles is a gated waterfront community in North Palm Beach. Some public records label the Gretzky property as West Palm Beach, which is why you will see both names in coverage. The neighborhood covers about 76 acres and is known for Mediterranean-style estates built between 2000 and 2004. One listing describes fewer than 100 homes and a manned gate.Boating is the main draw. Listings for the community advertise deep-water docks and ocean access with no fixed bridges, so a yacht can reach open water without waiting on a drawbridge. Prices across the community have ranged from $475,000 for the smallest units to $8.75 million for the priciest houses on one brokerage's site. A rare pair of adjoining homes on Harbour Isles Court was recently offered together at $19.95 million.That range explains the Gretzky result. Buyers here are not buying a generic mansion. They are buying a specific lot, a specific dock and a specific stretch of water. The Gretzky lot is 0.34 acres, which is modest by the standards of Florida estates. Buyers pay a premium for frontage and dock space, and not every house in the neighborhood has the same amount of either.How the sale fits Gretzky's long history with real estateThis is not the first time the Gretzkys have turned a property into a decent return. They bought a home at Sherwood Country Club in Los Angeles in 2009 for $2.765 million and later sold it for $6 million. Gretzky's family foundation also bought a townhouse in Palm Beach Gardens for $1.58 million in October 2021, a few months before the Harbour Isles deal.Family ties run through the Florida market, too. Johnson and Paulina Gretzky, Wayne's daughter, sold their own Palm Beach Gardens estate for a reported $16.5 million after buying it for about $5 million in 2015. Johnson and Paulina share two sons, Tatum and River.Gretzky has also been linked to homes in McCall, Idaho, and his childhood hometown of Brantford, Ontario. Whether the Harbour Isles sale signals a change in his Florida plans has not been stated. What the numbers do show is a family that has bought carefully, held for years, and sold into a market that was willing to pay.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Atlanta’s dream of a WNBA title might be coming soon. A guardian Angel leads the way
articles.summary: More than 17,000 Atlanta fans roared their Dream team to a thumping 26-point victory and a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals series against the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body: If you believe the polls, there is talk of a blue wave in the midterm elections next month. There was certainly a sky-blue wave in Atlanta on Wednesday night. More than 17,000 Atlanta fans roared the Dream to a thumping 26-point victory and a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals series against the Golden State Valkyries. There was barely any other color visible in a sold-out crowd at the State Farm Arena, and the noise was deafening from start to finish. Having watched their team level the series with a dominant performance on the road, the Atlanta crowd was fired up to welcome the Dream back to an arena that has quickly become their home, and it is now the only place in town that can accommodate such a rapidly expanding franchise. For a moment, it seemed as though this might instead have all played out 10 miles to the south of the city, in a claustrophobic arena outside Atlanta that the Dream have rapidly outgrown. Given what the scene at State Farm Arena on Wednesday was like, that would have been a travesty. They’re only halfway to the title, but this performance felt like a celebration befitting the size of the venue. Since 2021, Atlanta’s women have been playing out of a venue that can hold just 3,500 fans. Once they made the playoffs this season, they switched to State Farm, where much bigger crowds have cheered them to two straight sweeps on their way to the Finals. By the time they reached their first Finals since 2013, they’d won 10 straight games. During that run, the team announced that State Farm would become their permanent residency from 2027, but in the meantime, nobody knew where they would play the Finals. A concert was booked for the night of Game 3 and the city’s NBA team, the Hawks, were scheduled to play their home season opener on the night of Game 4. Atlanta’s fans were incensed, with many unfairly criticizing the Hawks – a franchise which hasn’t won the NBA Finals since 1961 and never since moving to Atlanta, it was noted with some derision. But thankfully a solution was found; Game 3 was brought forward by 24 hours and Game 4 will tip off at State Farm as a Saturday afternoon game, and Game 6, if it’s required … well, they’ll cross that bridge if they come to it. On Thursday, the musician Sombr will take the stage at State Farm Arena. On Wednesday, the mood was gleefully electric as Atlanta comprehensively dismantled their opponents to take control of the series. The whole scene was yet more evidence of a league that is absolutely booming. Prior to tipoff, NBC reported an average audience for 2.1 million viewers for Game 1, a new broadcast record, and the secondary ticket marketplace TickPick said that it was selling tickets for over $200 was also a Finals record. That’s despite the series missing arguably the game’s biggest stars. Caitlin Clark, the generational talent who propelled professional women’s basketball into the national consciousness in 2024, is nowhere near it. Neither is the league’s hottest player, the record five-time MVP A’Ja Wilson, whose defending champion Las Vegas were swept in the semifinals by Golden State. Those Aces were trumped in the semifinals by the dominant Valkyries, who’ve had the audacity to reach the Finals in only their second season. The Dream, meanwhile, are trying to bring some sporting pride to a city that so often has been also-rans or nowhere-nears. The league will crown a new champion at the end of the series. The ascendent Angel Reese Before this season, the Dream had played in three WNBA Finals and lost every single game. But this year is different, thanks in large part to the energetic and undeniably unapologetic Angel Reese. Once cast by some observers as the villain to Clark’s heroine, Reese has fought her way to the front of the pack and is now hoping to bask in the game’s brightest spotlight alone. In Game 2, she made history as the youngest player in WNBA history to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a postseason game. Only two other players, Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones, had ever done it in a Finals game. On Wednesday, she led the way again with another double -double. Since moving to Atlanta five months ago, Reese has established herself as the league’s defensive player of the year, but she is dangerous everywhere. In Game 3, the pink flashes on her sneakers were constantly visible as she constantly disrupted the Valkyries, leading all scorers with 21 points and 12 rebounds, often emoting in celebration with exuberant defiance. But this was a balanced, team performance from Atlanta; Naz Hillman, wearing 00 on her shirt, poured in a series of 3-point shots before moving in to inflict further damage from point-blank range, marksmanship that James Bond’s 007 would have been proud of. Isobel Borlase and Rhyne Howard kept the fans on their feet with huge blocks late in the third quarter to keep the Valkyries at arm’s length, literally. It was an historic night for Howard, who became the first player in Finals history to make five of more steals in consecutive games. After a 14-point road win in Game 2, a 97-71 victory was emphatic and Atlanta have built up the kind of momentum that might just be unstoppable. The Atlanta Dream might now be the hottest ticket in town and State Farm Arena would be fools not to host them in Game 6. But they’ve become such a nightmare for their opponents; this series one might be over in five.
